### Backstory: Julian Thorne
Julian Thorne is a 34-year-old former architect who specialized in urban revitalization projects. Two years ago, he was driving home from a high-stakes meeting when he experienced a severe panic attack that caused him to swerve and hit a parked car. Though no one was physically injured, the incident shattered his confidence. Since then, he has been unable to drive, resigned from his firm, and retreated into a state of chronic, paralyzing anxiety. He feels a deep sense of shame for leaving behind his career and his wife, Elena, who has been supportive but whom Julian feels he is failing daily. He suffers from persistent insomnia, dreads the mornings, and feels like a ghost living in his own home. He is visiting Dr. Aris because his wife insisted, and he feels he has run out of options.

***

### 100 Statements from Julian to Dr. Aris

**The Opening & Initial Hesitation**
1. "I didn't think I’d actually walk through the door today."
2. "My wife, Elena, said if I didn't come, she’d make the appointment for me."
3. "Are you going to write all of this down? It makes me feel like a lab rat."
4. "I feel like I’m wasting your time talking about feelings when I should be working."
5. "Where do I even start? It all feels like one big, tangled mess."
6. "I feel like an imposter even sitting in this chair."
7. "Does everyone look as tired as I feel when they come here?"
8. "I’m sorry, I just need a second to catch my breath."
9. "This room is very quiet. It makes me nervous."
10. "Can we talk about something else? I don't want to start with the crash again."

**On the Accident & Trauma**
11. "Every time I close my eyes, I see the headlights hitting the brick wall."
12. "I keep replaying the sound of the metal crunching over and over."
13. "I’m not afraid of dying; I’m afraid of losing control like that again."
14. "People told me I was 'lucky' no one was hurt, but that just makes me feel more guilty."
15. "I sold my car three months ago because looking at it in the garage made me vomit."
16. "I walk everywhere now, even if it’s miles, just to avoid being behind a wheel."
17. "The intersection where it happened—I take a two-mile detour just to avoid passing it."
18. "I feel like a defective machine that broke down and can’t be repaired."
19. "Sometimes I wonder if I hit that car because I subconsciously wanted to stop everything."
20. "Do you think PTSD ever really goes away, or do you just learn to carry it?"

**On Anxiety & Physical Symptoms**
21. "My chest feels like there’s a lead weight resting on it from the moment I wake up."
22. "I checked the locks on the front door four times before I left the house this morning."
23. "Does your heart ever just pound for no reason? Like it might explode?"
24. "I can’t breathe properly when the room is too small."
25. "I have these cold sweats at 3:00 AM, and I don't even know what I’ve been dreaming."
26. "I worry about everything—did I leave the stove on, will I lose my health insurance, is Elena leaving me?"
27. "The noise of the refrigerator feels like it’s vibrating inside my skull."
28. "My hands shake whenever I have to talk to a stranger."
29. "I feel like an animal trapped in a cage, but the cage is my own skin."
30. "Why is my body betraying me like this?"

**On Depression & Emptiness**
31. "I don’t remember the last time I felt genuine excitement."
32. "I look in the mirror and I don't recognize the person looking back."
33. "Everything feels gray, like I’m watching my life through a dirty window."
34. "I sleep for twelve hours and still wake up feeling exhausted."
35. "I just don’t see the point of anything today."
36. "Is this it? Is this the rest of my life?"
37. "I spend most of my days just staring at the wall, waiting for the sun to go down."
38. "I feel like a ghost haunting my own living room."
39. "Everything I used to love—architecture, sketching, reading—it all tastes like ash now."
40. "I feel completely hollowed out."

**On Work & Loss of Identity**
41. "I miss my desk. I miss solving actual problems."
42. "My coworkers email me to ask for advice on projects, and I just delete them."
43. "I feel like a failure because I’m a 34-year-old man who can’t hold down a job."
44. "I used to build skylines; now I can’t even build the courage to go to the store."
45. "I saw one of my old buildings on the way here and I had to turn away."
46. "Does my professional background matter if I’m just a broken person?"
47. "I keep waiting for my 'ambition' to come back, but it’s completely dead."
48. "I’m terrified that I’ve forgotten how to be competent."
49. "I feel like I lost the best version of myself in that crash."
50. "What if I’m never good at anything again?"

**On Relationships & Isolation**
51. "Elena tries so hard, and I just push her away."
52. "She looks at me with pity, and it makes me want to scream."
53. "I’m convinced she’ll eventually realize she’d be happier without me."
54. "I hide in the bathroom for twenty minutes just to avoid making conversation."
55. "I feel so lonely even when I’m sitting right next to her."
56. "I haven’t spoken to my parents in a month, and I honestly don't have the energy to lie to them."
57. "I feel like I’m a burden to everyone I love."
58. "They don’t get it; they think I’m just 'lazy' or 'needing a break.'"
59. "It’s hard to let someone help you when you don't even like yourself."
60. "I’m afraid I’m teaching my dog to be anxious, too."

**On Medication & Treatment**
61. "I really don’t want to take pills. I don't want to be 'numbed out'."
62. "What if the medication changes who I am?"
63. "I tried that SSRI years ago and it made me feel like an ice cube."
64. "Will this help with the intrusive thoughts, or just the sadness?"
65. "I’m scared that if I start taking medicine, I’ll never be able to stop."
66. "How long does it take until you feel... normal?"
67. "Is it addictive? I don't want to trade one problem for another."
68. "Will I still be able to feel happiness if I take these, or just 'flat'?"
69. "I read the side effects online, and they terrified me."
70. "I just want to be sharp again. I can’t afford to be foggy."

**On Fears & The Future**
71. "I’m terrified of my own potential for collapse."
72. "What if I get worse? What if this is just the beginning?"
73. "I’m scared that I’ll lose my mind entirely."
74. "Every time I make a plan for the future, I imagine it going wrong."
75. "I don’t know what I want for the future because I can’t get past tomorrow."
76. "I feel like I’m falling off a cliff and there’s nothing to grab onto."
77. "Maybe I’m just fundamentally flawed. Maybe I was born this way."
78. "I worry that I’ll wake up at 50 and realize I wasted my best years in this state."
79. "What if I never drive again? Is that a valid life?"
80. "Everything feels big and scary, and I feel small."

**On Self-Worth & Inner Dialogue**
81. "I tell myself I’m worthless at least twenty times a day."
82. "I hear this voice in my head that tells me I deserve to be stuck like this."
83. "Why can’t I just 'get over it' like everyone else does?"
84. "I feel so ashamed that I’m struggling when others have it much worse."
85. "I keep comparing myself to where I ‘should’ be."
86. "Is it selfish to feel this way?"
87. "I think I’m a coward."
88. "I’m exhausted by my own brain."
89. "I feel like I’m just waiting for the other shoe to drop all the time."
90. "I hate that I’ve become this version of myself."

**Closing Thoughts & Desperation**
91. "I’m running out of things to tell you."
92. "Is there actually a way out, or are we just managing the symptoms?"
93. "I’m tired of talking. I just want to feel like a human being again."
94. "What happens if this doesn't work?"
95. "I feel like I’ve told you my whole life story and yet, you still don’t know the real me."
96. "Is it okay to end the session early? I’m feeling overwhelmed."
97. "I’m sorry I’m so difficult."
98. "Thank you for listening, I guess. It’s... different than I expected."
99. "I’ll try to come back next week, but I can’t promise anything."
100. "I just want to know—is it possible to be 'okay' again?"
